CAT simulations

Polish WG Comprehension

Setup

Do not change the code or text in the document, unless you know what you are doing or you encounter an explicit encouragement to tweak code or settings. No modifications should be required to run the code (and eventually knit the document), as long as you successfully run the IRT model fitting for this dataset first.

The following libraries are loaded.

library(beepr)
library(tidyverse)
library(mirtCAT)
library(parallel)

Functions from “Functions” directory are sourced. Data are expected and saved in “Data” directory.

Data loading

There are four key objects needed for all the analyses done and presented here:

  1. IRT model (mod)
  2. responses matrix (administrations x items; 0/1), used for the final model (mod) fitting
  3. cdi data frame (items with their definitions & glosses), used for the final model (mod) fitting
  4. scores data frame (participant information: raw scores & demographics)

Model exploration

The model was fit to 366 items and 1381 administrations.

Simulations

At the moment the simulations we run help us to decide two stopping criteria for CAT, max. \(SE_{\theta}\) accepted and max. number of items allowed. We first observe how adding items decreases the mean \(SE_{\theta}\) and we identify the \(SE_{\theta}\) value, for which adding another item doesn’t result in a substantial drop anymore. Then we run simulations with that value as a stopping criterion to see how many items are needed to reach this criterion for a reasonably high proportion of administrations.

SE_delta <- 0.001 # non-substantial drop in mean SE
q_fail <- .2 # reasonably low proportion of administrations not reaching desired SE

Whole pool for everyone

We simulate CAT administrations without any stopping criteria (and save the simulation results to “Data/polish_wg_comp_sim_all.RData” for later reuse).

## Mean length: 366; Median length: 366
## Correlation with all-item thetas: 1, with raw scores: 0.895
## Mean SE: 0.099; Reliability: 0.99
## Never used items: 0 out of all 366

Based on the whole pool simulation we can examine decreasing average \(SE_{\theta}\) with each item.

We want to find the first average \(SE_{\theta}\) for which the difference between it and the next one is less than 0.001.

We plot the average \(SE_{\theta}\) by each consecutive item (max. 100: highly unlikely not to reach the plateau by then) and add red dashed lines marking the value identified above.

We can export the data for crosslinguistic plotting/analysing.

\(SE_{\theta} <\) 0.153 stop criterion

We take 0.153 as the max. \(SE_{\theta}\) we accept for a CAT administration (STOP CRITERION 1). Now we simulate CAT again, this time stopping each administration when its \(SE_{\theta}\) reaches this threshold.

## Mean length: 85.4; Median length: 19
## Correlation with all-item thetas: 0.979, with raw scores: 0.87
## Mean SE: 0.173; Reliability: 0.97
## Never used items: 0 out of all 366

We want to see the distribution of the number of items needed to reach it (and the proportion of administrations that will not reach it at all).

NB: If the histogram below doesn’t look ok, here are some settings you can modify.

bin_width <- 10
pfs <-  6   # font size for percentages above bars
xfs <-  14  # font size for bin labels on X axis

We want to find the number of items needed to leave only 0.2 of all administrations not reaching \(SE_{\theta} <\) 0.153.

## 80% 
## 122

We take 122 as the max. number of items we allow for a single CAT administration (STOP CRITERION 2).

Config files preparation

For the CAT app to work we need two files, items.csv with parameter estimates and a question for each item, and startThetas.csv with \(\theta_0\), either a single value or different values for different (combinations of) demographic (age and/or sex) variables.

\(\theta_0\) values may be “corrected” (i.e., decreased by a set constant) to make it more likely for first items to be answered positively.

“Questions” for individual items may be used to display for each item its category, but they may also be more specific (which is important for gestures but might be helpful to keep track of the comprehension/production distinction as well).

The code chunk below, if run, creates two files: “Data/polish_wg_comp_items.csv” and “Data/polish_wg_comp_startThetas.csv”.

start_thetas <- get_start_thetas(scores, "age", "sex", correction=.5)[[1]]
prepare_config_files(params_mirt, cdi$item_definition, fscores_aggr,
                     question = "CATEGORY LABEL here", group = subscale, id = cdi$item_id,
                     file1 = paste(filename_prefix, "items.csv", sep = "_"),
                     file2 = paste(filename_prefix, "startThetas.csv", sep = "_"))
